observations: Photo 0: Black Nikon DSLR camera with "Nikon" logo on the top prism, mounted with a large telephoto zoom lens, resting on a white McSteve Gadget Store box.
Photo 1: Lens barrel clearly reads "Nikon AF-P DX NIKKOR 70-300mm 1:4.5-6.3G ED VR"; camera body shows mode dial and buttons but the body model number is not legible.
Photo 2: Side/rear view showing scuffing on the handgrip, camera strap attached, same 70-300mm lens; "Nikon" logo visible on top.

identity.kind: DSLR camera with telephoto zoom lens

claims.evidence: Nikon logo is visible in photos 0-2, but the D3400 model number is not legible in any photo.

claims.claim: working perfectly ok with no fault
claims.evidence: Photos cannot show camera or lens function.

risks.risk: Camera body may not power on or function (shutter, buttons, sensor, autofocus).
risks.proof: Video of the camera turning on, navigating menus, and taking a photo.

risks.risk: Lens autofocus, zoom, or vibration reduction may be faulty.
risks.proof: Video of the lens zooming through its range and focusing.

risks.risk: Shutter may be worn or near end of life.
risks.proof: Shutter count reading from a test photo or seller-provided data.

risks.risk: Sensor, mirror, or internal components may be damaged.
risks.proof: Close-up of the sensor/mirror or a sample image straight from the camera.

proof_requests: Video of camera powering on and taking a photo
Video of lens zooming and focusing
Shutter count or sample photo from the camera
response.reason: The item is identifiable from the photos as a Nikon DSLR with a 70-300mm lens; even if untested, it can be priced at its worst case using the closest comparable body.
